title: Touch loop e2e: warp-leg flake + land leg + legs 6–10 — touch-loop.spec.ts fully green
description: Pick up TASK-95 (PRD §4.13, SC-6 — the SC-1 loop driven ENTIRELY by touch on the mobile profile) where the third attempt left it (handoff: `.ralph/split/TASK-95/handoff.md` — the split moved it from `.ralph/handoff/TASK-95.md`; read it FIRST, it carries the full diagnosis plan). Everything up to commit 4c7b84e is DONE and committed: the spec `app/tests/e2e/touch-loop.spec.ts` (714 lines, 8 legs), the optional `vel` on the dev teleport route in `app/src/server/routes/dev.ts`, the egress wiring in main.tsx, and the steering-free dead-stick land leg. Three known reds remain: (1) the WARP-LEG FLAKE — the ESC menu (z-index 111, later in the DOM than the star chart) intercepts Playwright's hit test on the chart node click; (2) the LAND LEG — the seeded 85 m / 50 m / 90 u/s dead-stick glide grounds at ~25 m (just OUTSIDE the 20 m pad disc) at speed 0, and the VTOL lift demonstrably never engaged server-side (prime suspect: the client's active control scheme is stale 'space' after the atmosphere teleport); (3) LEGS 6–10 (exit → mine → re-enter → sell) have NEVER executed. THIS TASK makes the spec FULLY GREEN in one run: fix the warp flake in-spec (2 lines), get the land leg to dock (the handoff's ordered diagnosis of the VTOL non-engagement under a HARD 15-minute time-box, else the bounded fallback: a closer start distance that docks on position/speed alone), then work legs 6–10 to green (first-touch fixes, spec-side). The ONE allowed product change is the land-leg regime-wiring fix in main.tsx, and only if the diagnosis proves it is a local wiring bug. NO docs, NO full gate, NO close-out bookkeeping — that is TASK-95.2. Ends with `npx tsc --noEmit` green, the spec green with its screenshot rewritten, and one wip commit.

steps.details:
In `app/tests/e2e/touch-loop.spec.ts`: `await padNode.click();` (line ~540) → `await padNode.click({ force: true });` and `await warpButton.click();` (line ~543) → `await warpButton.click({ force: true });`. Add a one-line comment explaining why: the co-open ESC menu shares z-index 111 with the star chart and renders LATER in the DOM (`openChart()` in `src/client/state/menu.ts:80` PUSHES the chart onto the surface stack without popping the menu; `#esc-menu` at `esc-menu.tsx:66` vs `#star-chart` at `star-chart.tsx:210`), so Playwright's hit test reports the menu's `

` intercepting the node. Do NOT change the app's surface-stack behaviour (that is TASK-53 semantics — the spec's intent is 'MENU → chart → warp by touch', the menu being co-open is the real touch flow). touch-menu.spec.ts (TASK-94, green) got lucky with node placement — leave it alone.

steps.description: Land leg: diagnose the VTOL non-engagement (time-boxed), then dock
steps.details: Run the spec once first to confirm the state: `cd app && npx playwright test touch-loop.spec.ts --config playwright.e2e.config.ts --reporter=line` (~6 min per run; expected: warp + space legs green post force-click, land leg red at the 25 s per-attempt timeout with `regime=sublight dist≈25 m alt≈1 m speed≈0.0` — the run-5 state). Then, in order, under a HARD 15-minute budget for the whole diagnosis: (a) Add an INPUT-FRAME tap inside `tapShipUpdates` (the WebSocket constructor monkey-patch already in the spec): also intercept `send`, parse the envelopes, and record payloads with `type === 'input'` into `window.__TLIN__`; in the vtol probe log the last few sent frames' `up`/`thrust` values — this shows EXACTLY what the client put on the wire when VTOL was pressed. (b) Find where the client picks its active scheme: grep `regimeWiring` in `app/src/client/main.tsx` (~line 1851: `flightScheme = docked || regime === 'surface'` → character scheme, else `remapper.readInput`) and determine whether a SERVER teleport that puts the ship in the atmosphere updates it without a locally-predicted boundary crossing (the wire `flightRegime` IS 'atmosphere' — the spec's poll passed — so if the client scheme is still 'space', the remapper reads through the SPACE scheme where `vtol: null` → `up: 0` on the wire; input chain: `src/client/input/touch.ts` → `src/client/input/controls.ts` `readSchemeInput` → main.tsx flight loop ~1834–1893 → `shard.enqueueInput`). (c) If the scheme is stale and the fix is LOCAL (the remapper must follow the SERVER-reported flightRegime, which snapshots carry, even when the client predictor never crossed the boundary locally): apply it in main.tsx — a legit wiring fix (the parent task says fix the responsible wiring, not special-case the loop). Constraint: it must not change the default keyboard / no-touch path (server, wire mapping, prediction and the golden flight fixtures stay untouched — TASK-95.2's full unit gate verifies the fixtures are bit-identical). (d) FALLBACK — use it if the diagnosis exceeds the 15-minute box, or the fix is not local: make docking not depend on the VTOL lift at all — lower `LAND_START_DIST_M` from 85 to 55–60 (keep `LAND_START_ALT_M = 50`, `LAND_INBOUND_M_S = 90`) so the drag-limited glide stops INSIDE the 20 m disc; docking is position/speed-based (`satisfiesDock` in `src/shared/world/pads.ts`: surface regime + |vel.y| < 2 + ≤ 20 m + ≤ 1 m alt), so a grounded, slow ship inside the disc docks with NO vtol. Keep the vtol switch + dive probe as-is (fast path when the lift works; the probe keeps proving the channel reaches the server). Physics references: `app/src/server/shard/shard.pads.approach.test.ts` (the proven 100 m/50 m → 90 u/s → docked-in-4.5 s on the REAL SimLoop), `app/src/shared/physics/flight.ts` (`VTOL_LIFT = 1.35·GRAVITY`, `VTOL_HORIZONAL_LIMIT = 5`, atmosphere has NO main thruster). Then re-run the spec: the land leg must dock (`#docked-indicator` visible within 15 s of the state machine settling).

steps.description: Legs 6–10: exit → mine → re-enter → sell — spec FULLY GREEN
steps.details: Once the land leg docks, legs 6–10 have NEVER executed — expect first-touch issues and iterate (6 min per run). They reuse proven patterns verbatim: (7) egress via the shared `interactPress` (committed in main.tsx by `162bdec`); (8) mine — `walkUntilPrompt` to the seeded deposit (the copy is verbatim from the green `touch-onfoot.spec.ts`), then a FULL `interactPress` hold (> 1.5 s server mining channel) → `interactRelease` → weight bar `1/40u` (interact.spec.ts pattern); (9) re-enter — `walkUntilPrompt` to `[E] Enter ship`, prompt holds, `interactPress` → docked HUD stubs return + on-foot layout gone (enter-ship.spec.ts pattern); (10) sell — second egress → `walkUntilPrompt` to `[E] Dock terminal` → `interactPress` → `#dock-panel` → TAP `button[aria-label="sell all iron inv"]` → credits 500 → 505 cr + bar `0/40u` (sell.spec.ts terminal condition). Fix spec-side: timeouts, prompt strings, walk bursts, settles. NO product code changes in this step — if a leg reveals a real product bug, stop, record it in the handoff, and do not silently special-case around it. Green bar: the WHOLE spec passes in ONE run — all 8 legs + `collectErrors().assertClean()` (zero unhandled console errors across the entire loop) + the screenshot `.ralph/screenshots/TASK-95-1.png` rewritten at the sold/dock state + the `[TASK-95] loop wall=…s` console line printed — CAPTURE THAT WALL-TIME VALUE (TASK-95.2 records it in the LOG entry; put it in your commit message too).

`cd app && npx tsc --noEmit` green. Remove temporary ad-hoc probes — the `__TLIN__` input-frame tap is fine to KEEP (small, commented, a permanent diagnostic aid); anything else must go, and the spec diff must read clean. Update the handoff (`.ralph/split/TASK-95/handoff.md`, or `.ralph/handoff/TASK-95.md` if the split left it there) to a short note: spec fully green, which land-leg fix was taken (wiring vs closer-start fallback), the loop wall time, and 'remaining: TASK-95.2 (docs + full gate + close-out)'. Commit ONLY the task's files (spec + any main.tsx wiring fix + the rewritten screenshot + the handoff): `wip(TASK-95): touch-loop e2e fully green (warp force-click; land leg = <wiring fix | closer-start fallback>; legs 6-10; loop wall=…s)`. Exclude every pre-existing dirty file (see notes).

acceptanceCriteria: touch-loop.spec.ts FULLY GREEN in one run: the SC-1 loop (claim → MENU/chart/warp → space thrust+yaw → atmosphere land at the pad → exit → mine 1/40u → re-enter → sell 505 cr / 0/40u) driven ENTIRELY through the touchDebug channels + DOM taps on React buttons on the mobile profile — zero keyboard/mouse input — with assertClean() passing and .ralph/screenshots/TASK-95-1.png rewritten at the sold/dock state

The land leg docks (`#docked-indicator` + pad regime) — via the regime-wiring fix (only if the diagnosis proves it local) or the closer-start fallback; no facePad/steering resurrection; server / wire / golden fixtures untouched (at most the main.tsx wiring fix)
npx tsc --noEmit green; no temporary probes left; one wip commit with only the task's files; handoff updated with the loop wall time and the land-leg fix taken
The warp-leg flake is gone: the chart node + WARP button clicks use force:true with the z-index/DOM-order comment
notes: DONE (committed — do NOT redo): `162bdec` = spec written (claim→warp→space legs green) + egress moved into the shared `interactPress`; `04f3f89` = flightRegime tap fix (wire `regime` is docked/sublight, `flightRegime` is space/atmosphere/surface — `entityToState` ~line 4239 in `app/src/server/shard/shard.ts`) + first land rewrite; `4c7b84e` = steering-free dead-stick land leg + optional `vel` on `POST /api/dev/teleport` (zod .strict extended, passed to `shard.teleportForTesting` which supported it since TASK-32; dev-only route). Working tree at start: CLEAN for all task files — nothing to salvage.

DEAD ENDS — do not retry: (a) facePad steering (aim/face after the atmosphere teleport) — the ship never rotated on touch yaw/pitch post-teleport while the same channels work in space; RESOLVED BY DESIGN (the land leg does no steering). (b) 60 m straight drop onto the pad — free-falls into the 20 m disc and the pad machine re-docks instantly → the atmosphere poll can't observe 'atmosphere'. (c) 300 m / 150 m start with thrust — the atmosphere regime has NO main thruster (only drag/gravity/VTOL-lift in `flight.ts integrateStep`), so the close phase could never build inbound speed. (d) 85 m start at 90 u/s — glides in and stops at ~25 m, just outside the disc, speed 0 (the run-5 state this task fixes via the step-2 diagnosis/fallback).

The land-leg red (run 5): `land leg attempt 1 timed out (regime=sublight dist=25 m alt=1 m speed=0.0 u/s)` — the vtol switch DID fire per the flag logic (the miss-check is skipped once `vtolHeld` is set), yet a held VTOL (1.35·g lift) cannot end in a grounded speed-0 rest → the server never applied it. The unit-test approach (100 m/50 m, 90 u/s) docks at ~13 m on the SAME SimLoop, so the delta is client/scheme-related, not physics.

The warp-leg flake (run 6): died at `padNode.click()` — `

The world keeps moving while the menu is open.

… intercepts pointer events` (screenshot `app/test-results/…/test-failed-1.png` shows the ESC menu over the chart). In-spec fix = force clicks (step 1), NOT a surface-stack change.

Legs 6–10 context: `walkUntilPrompt` is verbatim from the green `touch-onfoot.spec.ts` (prompt-as-sensor steering loop, nudge-sign convention `dir = angle > 0 ? -1 : 1`, charSettled after every burst); the egress legs use the committed main.tsx `interactPress` fix; mine/re-enter/sell follow interact.spec.ts / enter-ship.spec.ts / sell.spec.ts patterns.

Commands: spec = `cd app && npx playwright test touch-loop.spec.ts --config playwright.e2e.config.ts --reporter=line` (~6 min per run; the e2eServer fixture boots its own dev server — NEVER run alongside `npm run dev`); typecheck = `cd app && npx tsc --noEmit`. Timing budget (45 min): warp fix ~2 min; confirm run ~6 min; diagnosis (grep/read/tap) ≤ 15 min (HARD BOX — then take the fallback); fix + run ~11 min; legs 6–10 1–2 runs ~12 min; tsc + handoff + commit ~5 min.
